bib.title: InstructRetro: Instruction Tuning post Retrieval-Augmented Pretraining

read.skipped: reference list skimmed; Appendix Faiss ablation table (Table 6/7) read as prose only

question: Does retrieval-augmented pretraining at 48B scale, followed by instruction tuning, give a better zero-shot decoder than the same GPT instruction-tuned and used with RAG?
hypothesis: Scaling Retro to 48B and instruction-tuning it mitigates the zero-shot generalization gap; retrieval pretraining improves in-context use of evidence.
contributions: Retro 48B, the largest LLM pretrained with retrieval
InstructRetro 48B outperforms instruction-tuned GPT with RAG on zero-shot tasks
The Retro encoder can be ablated: the decoder-only InstructRetro 43B gives comparable results

method.summary: Continue pretraining a 43B GPT (1.1T tokens) for 100B more tokens with Retro chunk-wise cross-attention over a 1.2T-token database, unfreezing the decoder; instruction-tune with the encoder gate off; compare with GPT-fitting + instruction tuning (InstructGPT-RAG 43B) zero-shot.
method.task: zero-shot QA, long-form QA, summarization with retrieved context

datasets.name: Pretraining corpus
datasets.source: Common Crawl, news, conversational, books, Wikipedia, ROOTS

datasets.name: Instruction tuning blend
datasets.source: SODA, ELI5, Self-Instruct, Unnatural Instructions, FLAN/CoT, OpenAssistant, Dolly, private conversations, pretraining samples

models.name: Retro 48B
models.architecture: GPT 43B decoder + 2-layer bidirectional encoder + chunk-wise cross-attention

training.objective: language modelling; instruction tuning loss on last assistant response only
training.compute: 69995 GPU hours Retro 48B vs 53329 GPU hours GPT 43B on 100B tokens

other.overall_extra_cost: 2.58% more GPU hours than GPT 43B on 1.2T tokens

inference.retrieval: DRAGON+ retriever, top-k=5 neighbors concatenated in the prompt for NQ, TriviaQA, doc2dial and long-form QA; provided contexts for other tasks. Pretraining: BERT embeddings, 19B chunks of 64 tokens, top-k=2 neighbors, Faiss

metrics.name: EM / F1 / ROUGE
metrics.definition: exact match, F1, geometric mean of ROUGE-1/2/L

eval.protocol: single runs; no significance tests reported

results.claim: Retro 48B reaches lower perplexity than GPT 43B for only 2.58% extra GPU hours.
results.setup: Retro-fitting a 43B GPT for 100B tokens vs GPT 43B on 1.2T tokens
results.quote: Retro 48B only need 2.58% additional GPU hours than its counterpart GPT trained on 1.2T tokens

results.claim: Retro perplexity beats GPT models with 4x larger parameter sizes, and the gap does not shrink from 8B to 48B.
results.quote: Retro achieves even better perplexity than GPT models with 4× larger parameter sizes.
results.note: read from Figure 2; no table of values

results.quote: the average relative improvement of In-structRetro across all the short-form datasets is around 7%

results.quote: such improvements further demonstrate the potential of retrieval-

results.claim: On three summarization datasets the average improvement is 16%, GovReport ROUGE 17.46 vs 12.59.
Dropping the Retro encoder costs nothing: InstructRetro 43B (decoder only) matches 48B with encoder (NQ 38.9 vs 38.6).
results.setup: Table 1, avg +7% w/o encoder vs +6% w/ encoder
results.table: Table 1, rows InstructRetro 43B and 48B, column NQ

results.claim: Before instruction tuning the retrieval benefit saturates with scale; instruction tuning unlocks it.
results.quote: We hypothesize that this saturation is mainly due to the poor instruction following
results.note: read from Figure 5; no numbers printed

results.claim: On MT-Bench the Tulu-v2 tuned InstructRetro 43B averages 6.70 vs 6.44 for InstructGPT 43B, lower on role play and coding.

limits: Instruction tuning ran with the encoder off because instruction data has no retrieved neighbours; retrieval-augmented instruction tuning is left as future work.
Retro 48B vs GPT 43B are not parameter-matched (about 10% extra parameters in encoder and cross-attention) and Retro costs about 31-37% more compute on the continued-pretraining tokens.
Single runs with no significance tests; three long-form datasets are proprietary.
Gains are smaller on TriviaQA (+0.26%) and negative on TriviaQA for the encoder variant (-0.38%); Retro is lower than GPT on role play and coding in MT-Bench.
Downstream retrieval uses task-specific corpora and DRAGON+, not the pretraining database, so the pretraining-time retriever (BERT) is never the one evaluated downstream.
